chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

Mecca is the sanctuary of Allah, the sanctuary of His Messenger, and the sanctuary of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). A prayer offered there is equivalent to one hundred thousand prayers, and a dirham spent there is equivalent to one hundred thousand dirhams, and a dinar spent there is equivalent to one hundred thousand dinars.

And Medina is the sanctuary of Allah, the sanctuary of His Messenger, and the sanctuary of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). A prayer offered there is equivalent to ten thousand prayers, and a dirham spent there is equivalent to ten thousand dirhams, and a dinar spent there is equivalent to ten thousand dinars.

And Kufa is the sanctuary of Allah the Exalted, the sanctuary of His Messenger, and the sanctuary of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). A prayer offered there is equivalent to one thousand prayers, and a dirham spent there is equivalent to one thousand dirhams, and a dinar spent there is equivalent to one thousand dinars.

key_terms.حَرَمُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: Sanctuary of Ali ibn Abi Talib

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual merit of praying and spending in Mecca, Medina, and Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchical sanctity among Mecca, Medina, and Kufa, designating Kufa as the specific 'Haram' (sanctuary) of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, thereby linking its spiritual merit directly to the presence of the first Imam. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on Kufa not merely as a historical capital but as a sacred locus of devotion, where acts of worship and charity yield multiplied rewards, reflecting the city's unique status in Islamic eschatology and jurisprudence.
